answer.rationale: Finance requires an 18% spend reduction, and the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. Memory c2 indicates the low-cost vendor previously delivered sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, which directly supports the cost mandate. Before committing, I want to verify c2 against the archived source to confirm the magnitude and durability of those savings and check for any caveat (quality, lead-time, or risk) that consolidated memory may have smoothed over. I will not verify c1 or c6 because renewal/incumbent strategies are inconsistent with the primary cost objective, and c4 (negotiating terms) is not a standalone action under the one-decision-per-cycle constraint when the low-cost vendor already meets the mandate. The assembly line at 94% utilization with no buffer raises delivery risk, but switching to an already-onboarded low-cost vendor with a verified track record is lower risk than staying with a soon-to-expire contract or adding a second source this cycle. Deferring the decision is not viable because the contract expires in 14 days and does not auto-renew; inaction means defaulting to a potentially unfavorable month-to-month or service gap.
